wu: Human Bingo: Students walk around with bingo cards containing facts like 'has a pet' or 'likes football'. They ask classmates 'Do you have a pet?' and mark squares if the answer is yes. First to get a line wins.
wuAlt: Two Truths and a Lie: Students write three statements about themselves, two true and one false. Partners guess which is the lie.
Name Chain: Students stand in a circle and say their name plus an adjective starting with the same letter (e.g., 'I'm Amazing Ali').
pres: Use flashcards showing people with different hobbies and nationalities. Model sentences: 'What's your name? I'm Ali. Where are you from? I'm from Morocco. How old are you? I'm 14.' Check understanding by asking students to repeat and translate the questions.
presAlt: Realia: Show objects representing hobbies (football, book, guitar) and ask 'What's your hobby?' Model answers with 'I like football.'
Dialogue: Read a short conversation between two teens meeting for the first time, highlighting the target questions and answers.
prac: Find Someone Who... worksheet with prompts like 'Find someone who speaks French.' Students walk around asking 'Do you speak French?' and writing names. Monitor and correct errors in question forms.
pracAlt: Question Cards: Students draw cards with Wh- questions (e.g., 'Where do you live?') and ask partners. Partners answer in full sentences.
Interview Relay: In pairs, Student A asks 3 questions, Student B answers, then they swap roles.
ls: Listen to a KET-style audio of two teens introducing themselves. Students complete a profile worksheet with details like name, age, and hobbies. Play twice for comprehension.
re: Stand Up Sit Down: Call out facts like 'Stand up if you have a sister.' Students stand or sit, practicing 'Do you have a sister?' responses.
prod: Group Poster Project: Groups of 3 create a poster titled 'Getting to Know Us' with 5 facts per member (e.g., 'Ali is 14 and likes football'). They present their poster to the class.
rw: Read a short KET-style profile about a teen named Sara. Answer 3 multiple-choice questions about her details (name, age, hobby). Then write a 40-word paragraph introducing yourself using the same structure.
st: Sing 'Hello, Hello' with actions. End with the goodbye routine: 'Today we learned to ask and answer getting-to-know-you questions. Thank you, class! Goodbye!'
g: Students mark squares on bingo cards when their classmates say facts matching the prompts.
Students sit in a circle and ask the next student a Wh- question, who answers and asks the next.
Students describe a classmate using 'He/She is...' and others guess who it is.
Students interview 3 different partners in 2 minutes each, writing down answers.
Students sit in a circle and say 'My name is [name] and I like [hobby]' each person repeats all previous names and hobbies.
diff: Fast finishers: Add a 6th question to their poster, e.g., 'What do you want to be in the future?'
Support weaker learners: Use sentence starters like 'My name is ___. I am ___ years old. I like ___.' on their worksheet.
hw: Record a 1-minute video introducing yourself with 5 facts (name, age, family, hobbies, future dream).
Write a 50-word paragraph about a new friend you met in class today.
Interview a family member in English and write down 3 things you learned about them.
tip: Encourage students to use Moroccan cultural references (e.g., 'I like couscous' or 'I celebrate Eid') to make personal connections and build confidence.
